items.note: Place 非常 directly before an adjective to express a high degree, meaning “very.” Learners may put 非常 after the adjective, but it does not work as a post-adjective intensifier in this pattern.

items.wrongPy: tā men hǎo fēi cháng
items.why: 非常 must come before the adjective; the correct sentence is 她们非常好。

items.wrongPy: hàn yǔ hǎo fēi cháng
items.why: 非常 must come before the adjective; the correct sentence is 汉语非常好。

items.note: Add 呢 to the end of a person or thing to ask “What about…?” as a follow-up to the conversation. Learners may put 呢 before the noun phrase, but in this pattern it belongs after the whole phrase.

items.wrongPy: ne nín
items.why: 呢 follows the person being asked about; say 您呢？

items.wrongPy: ne lǎo shī
items.why: 呢 belongs after 老师 in this follow-up question; say 老师呢？

items.wrongPy: ne tóng xué
items.why: 呢 must come after 同学 in this pattern; say 同学呢？

items.wrongPy: ne xué xiào
items.why: 呢 follows 学校 in this follow-up; say 学校呢？

items.en: What about a cup of tea?
items.wrongPy: yì bēi ne chá
items.why: 呢 cannot split the measure phrase from 茶 here; say 一杯茶呢？

items.wrongPy: ne hàn yǔ lǎo shī
items.why: 呢 comes after the complete noun phrase 汉语老师; say 汉语老师呢？

items.note: A contextual short expression can work as a complete utterance when the situation supplies what is left unsaid. Greetings, farewells, and brief replies often use this pattern; learners should not rearrange fixed expressions or move 吧 away from the verb phrase.

items.wrongPy: bàn diǎn liù
items.why: The time expression orders the hour before the half hour; the correct phrase is 六点半。

items.wrongPy: méi shì nǐ men ba shàng kè
items.why: 吧 follows the verb phrase as a suggestion; the correct order is 你们上课吧。

items.en: You're welcome. You all get some rest.
items.wrongPy: bú kè qi nǐ men dōu ba xiū xi
items.why: 吧 follows the verb phrase, not 都; the correct order is 你们都休息吧。

items.wrongPy: hěn hǎo mǐ fàn
items.why: The subject must precede its predicate; say 米饭很好。

items.wrongPy: fēi cháng hǎo tā men
items.why: The subject comes before the description; say 她们非常好。

items.en: That one is a little cold.
items.wrongPy: yǒu diǎnr lěng nà ge
items.why: The subject comes first; say 那个有点儿冷。

items.wrongPy: xué xí hàn yǔ hàn yǔ lǎo shī
items.why: The subject 汉语老师 must come before the verb; say 汉语老师学习汉语。

items.note: In a noun compound, the modifying noun comes before the head noun and specifies its type or topic, as in “Chinese teacher.” Use this pattern to form compact noun phrases. Learners may reverse the nouns; put the specifying noun first.

items.wrongPy: lǎo shī hàn yǔ ne
items.why: 汉语 specifies the kind of 老师 and comes first; say 汉语老师呢？

items.wrongPy: yī shēng nǚ
items.why: 女 comes before the head noun 医生; say 女医生。

items.wrongPy: hào fáng jiān shì sān hào
items.why: 房间 comes before 号 in this compound; say 房间号是三号。

items.wrongPy: wǒ xǐ huan gē zhōng guó
items.why: 中国 specifies 歌 and must come first; say 我喜欢中国歌。

items.wrongPy: rén zhōng guó xǐ huan dú shū
items.why: 中国 comes before 人 in this noun phrase; say 中国人喜欢读书。

items.wrongPy: lǎo shī hàn yǔ xué xí hàn yǔ
items.why: 汉语 comes before 老师 in the noun compound; say 汉语老师学习汉语。

items.note: Use 是 between a subject and a noun to identify or classify the subject. It links two noun phrases, as in “X is Y.” Learners may omit 是 or move it out of its place; keep it between the subject and the noun.

items.wrongPy: zhè wǒ
items.why: An identity statement needs 是 between 这 and 我; say 这是我。

items.wrongPy: nǐ ma shì lǎo shī
items.why: 吗 belongs at the end of the question; say 你是老师吗？

items.wrongPy: tóng xué nǐ men shì
items.why: Put the subject before 是 and the noun after it; say 你们是同学。

items.wrongPy: nǚ yī shēng tā shì
items.why: The subject must come before 是 and its noun; say 她是女医生。

items.wrongPy: fáng jiān hào sān hào shì
items.why: The noun after 是 completes the identity statement; say 房间号是三号。

items.note: In a basic verbal statement, put the verb phrase after the subject without 是. Use this pattern to describe actions or habits; learners often insert 是 before an ordinary action verb, confusing it with an identity statement.

items.wrongPy: wǒ tīng shì gē
items.why: 是 cannot go between 听 and its object here; say 我听歌。

items.wrongPy: tā hàn zì dú
items.why: The object cannot precede 读 in this basic statement; say 他读汉字。

items.wrongPy: tā men xiū xi dōu
items.why: 都 belongs before the verb here; say 她们都休息。

items.wrongPy: lǎo shī xué xí shì hàn yǔ
items.why: 是 cannot separate 学习 from its object here; say 老师学习汉语。

items.wrongPy: xià wǔ xiū xi wǒ men ba
items.why: The subject must precede the verb phrase; say 下午我们休息吧。

items.en: It’s okay; you all go rest.
items.wrongPy: méi guān xi nǐ men ba xiū xi
items.why: 吧 belongs at the end of the suggestion; say 没关系，你们休息吧。

items.note: Use 都 before the predicate to say that every member of the plural topic shares the same action or quality. Put it before 很 when 很 is present; learners often place 都 after the predicate or after 很.

items.wrongPy: wǒ men xiū xi dōu
items.why: 都 must precede the predicate; the correct order is 我们都休息。

items.wrongPy: tā men xué dōu zhōng wén
items.why: 都 precedes the verb, not the object; the correct sentence is 他们都学中文。

items.wrongPy: tā men shì dà xué shēng dōu
items.why: 都 must come before the predicate; the correct sentence is 她们都是大学生。

items.wrongPy: wǔ gè tóng xué xiū xi dōu
items.why: 都 must precede the predicate; the correct order is 五个同学都休息。

items.en: These primary school students are all very busy.
items.wrongPy: zhè xiē xiǎo xué shēng hěn dōu máng
items.why: 都 comes before 很, not after it; the correct sentence is 这些小学生都很忙。

items.en: All four daughters are very happy.
items.wrongPy: sì gè nǚ ér hěn dōu gāo xìng
items.why: 都 comes before 很, not after it; the correct sentence is 四个女儿都很高兴。

items.note: Put 不 immediately before a predicate to negate a habit, intention, or description. Use it for meanings such as “not heavy” or “don’t want”; learners often use 不 for possession or completed events, which require a different negation.

items.wrongPy: bù yǔ dà
items.why: 不 must precede the predicate, so the correct order is 雨不大。

items.wrongPy: wǒ bú nà ge yào
items.why: 不 cannot separate 这 kind of object from 要; say 我不要那个。

items.wrongPy: zhè xiē shū xīn bù
items.why: This is not a correct statement order; put 不 before 新, as in 这些书不新。

items.wrongPy: wǒ xué xí bú hàn yǔ
items.why: 不 belongs before the verb phrase, so say 我不学习汉语。

items.wrongPy: wǒ bú cài xǐ huan chī
items.why: 菜 cannot come before the verb phrase here; say 我不喜欢吃菜。

items.wrongPy: zhè ge bú wèn tí dà
items.why: 不 must precede the predicate 大, not split 这个问题; say 这个问题不大。

items.note: Put 有点儿 or 有一点儿 before an adjective to describe a somewhat unpleasant or undesirable degree. Learners often put it after the adjective; in this pattern, it must come first.

items.wrongPy: tā lěng yǒu diǎnr
items.why: 有点儿 must precede the adjective; the correct sentence is 她有点儿冷。

items.wrongPy: tā lěng yǒu diǎnr
items.why: 有点儿 must precede the adjective; the correct sentence is 他有点儿冷。

items.en: The water is a little cold.
items.wrongPy: shuǐ lěng yǒu diǎnr
items.why: 有点儿 must precede the adjective; the correct sentence is 水有点儿冷。

items.en: It is a little hot today.
items.wrongPy: jīn tiān rè yǒu diǎnr
items.why: 有点儿 must precede the adjective; the correct sentence is 今天有点儿热。

items.wrongPy: tā men jué de lěng yǒu yì diǎnr
items.why: 有一点儿 must precede the adjective; the correct sentence is 她们觉得有一点儿冷。

items.en: The university student feels a little cold.
items.wrongPy: dà xué shēng jué de lěng yǒu diǎnr
items.why: 有点儿 must precede the adjective; the correct sentence is 大学生觉得有点儿冷。

items.note: Add 吗 to the end of a statement to make a yes/no question, keeping the statement’s word order. Do not put 吗 inside the sentence. Learners often move it after the subject; place it only at the end.

items.wrongPy: nǐ ma zuò fàn
items.why: 吗 must end the question, not follow 你; say 你做饭吗？

items.wrongPy: nǐ shì ma lǎo shī
items.why: 吗 belongs at the end of the sentence; say 你是老师吗？

items.wrongPy: nǐ men le ma xià bān
items.why: 了吗 follows the verb 下班; say 你们下班了吗？

items.wrongPy: zhè ge dōng xi ma duì
items.why: 吗 comes after the statement; say 这个东西对吗？

items.wrongPy: tā men jīn tiān ma zuò fàn
items.why: 吗 must follow the predicate, not 今天; say 她们今天做饭吗？

items.en: Do you want to rest today?
items.wrongPy: jīn tiān nǐ ma yào xiū xi
items.why: 吗 belongs at the end of the question; say 今天你要休息吗？

items.note: A transitive verb comes before its object, including a noun phrase with a number and measure word. Use this for actions directed at something; learners often move the object before the verb.

items.en: I’d like three cups of tea.
items.wrongPy: sān bēi yào chá
items.why: 要 must precede the object 三杯茶; say 要三杯茶.

items.en: I want to buy new clothes.
items.wrongPy: wǒ mǎi xiǎng xīn yī fu
items.why: 想 must precede the action 买; say 我想买新衣服.

items.en: They drink five cups of milk.
items.wrongPy: tā men hē wǔ gè bēi niú nǎi
items.why: 个 cannot be stacked before 杯; the correct measure phrase is 五杯牛奶.

items.note: Mandarin time expressions usually come before the subject or after it but before the predicate. Use this to say when an action happens; learners often put the time between the verb and its object.

items.en: I drink tea in the afternoon.
items.wrongPy: xià wǔ hē chá wǒ
items.why: The subject must precede the predicate; say 下午我喝茶 or 我下午喝茶.

items.wrongPy: jīn tiān dōu tā men xiū xi
items.why: 都 follows its subject, so it belongs after 她们, not before it.

items.en: She comes to the bookstore to buy books in the afternoon.
items.wrongPy: xià wǔ lái shū diàn tā mǎi shū
items.why: The subject must come before 来书店; say 下午她来书店买书.

items.en: I can watch a movie tomorrow.
items.wrongPy: míng tiān kě yǐ wǒ kàn diàn yǐng
items.why: The subject must precede 可以; say 明天我可以看电影.

items.en: We are going to see a movie on Sunday.
items.wrongPy: xīng qī tiān qù wǒ men kàn diàn yǐng
items.why: The subject must precede 去; say 星期天我们去看电影.

items.note: Place 吧 at the end of a suggestion or softened request to invite agreement. It can make an instruction sound less direct; learners often place it before the verb or object instead of after the whole suggestion.

items.wrongPy: qǐng ba chī miàn bāo
items.why: 吧 belongs after the request, not before 吃; say 请吃面包吧。

items.en: Come over and find me soon.
items.wrongPy: kuài ba guò lái zhǎo wǒ
items.why: 吧 belongs after the complete suggestion; say 快过来找我吧。

items.wrongPy: jīn tiān wǒ men ba zuò fàn
items.why: 吧 must follow 做饭 in this suggestion; say 今天我们做饭吧。

items.en: It’s okay; you all go rest.
items.wrongPy: méi guān xi nǐ men ba xiū xi
items.why: 吧 belongs at the end of the softened request; say 没关系，你们休息吧。
